Aurore Marechal | Getty Images Disney reports quarterly earnings before the bell on Tuesday, and investors will be focused on the direction of the company's streaming and theme parks businesses — as well as further updates on CEO Josh D'Amaro's strategy for growth. Disney's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings will be released around eight months after D'Amaro took over for Bob Iger as CEO. In that time, the company has seen layoffs across divisions. The most recent round , which seeks to reduce costs by up to 20%, was reported earlier this month. Here's how Disney is expected to perform in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.67 expected Revenue : $25.18 billion expected In addition to updates on Disney's cost-cutting efforts, Wall Street will be keen for information about the company's subscriber base and advertising growth for Disney+, Hulu and ESPN's direct-to-consumer app. Investors once heavily scrutinized subscriber numbers, but Disney has stopped providing these figures on a quarterly basis. It also recently stopped reporting some metrics for its entertainment segment, such as a breakdown of revenue and operating income for its linear TV networks. Theme parks remain a driver of revenue and profit. But the effects of the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran and related jump in oil prices have affected some of Disney's peers. Last quarter, Disney said that despite these trends and broader uncertainty for consumers, demand at domestic parks remained healthy and there had been an increase in guest spending.
